findings.summary: apps/ui/src/workshopService.ts hand-authors a full parallel set of TypeScript interfaces (RegistrationFormDocument, WorkshopDetailDocument, OfferSummaryDocument, WaitlistFormDocument, etc.) that mirror the shapes of the UJG's authored JSON Schema data contracts field-for-field. They carry no behavioral logic and are not tool-generated, but they are a second, hand-maintained description of the same wire shapes the schemas already define, which is exactly the kind of duplication source_of_truth_integrity asks to watch for. A schema/version drift between the two would not be caught by any check in the run.

The manifest's domain_engine.runtime.version (>=22.5, needed because src/persistence/database.mjs imports the node:sqlite DatabaseSync API) is not reflected anywhere in the realized package metadata: the workspace root package.json only declares engines.node >=22, and apps/domain/package.json declares no engines field at all, so a Node 22.0-22.4 install would pass every declared engine constraint yet fail at runtime.

joinWaitlist() has an 'unsupported' outcome (workshop still advertises an available place, or the participant already holds a confirmed place) that is not part of the UJG's modeled workshop-participation outcome space (waitlisted/confirmed) or any JourneyExit. It is inert to the visible UI (the screen simply reloads the workshop's current situation) and is exercised by tests, but it is an implementation-invented outcome sitting outside what the UJG names.
